title: Commissioning workflow
summary: From installed hardware to a verified machine: configuration download, I/O check, function and fault tests.

sections.heading: Step by step
sections.body: Commissioning proves that the installation, the configuration and the program work together. It goes from power and hardware checks through the **I/O check** (every signal on the right tag) to function and fault tests and documentation.

sections.heading: The sequence
sections.body: Each step builds on the previous one.
sections.diagram: power check -> hardware config -> I/O check -> analog check -> function test -> fault tests -> handover

sections.heading: Loop check with forcing
sections.body: Force an output to confirm the actuator, then remove the force. **Safety:** on a real machine a forced output energizes the actuator regardless of the program and its interlocks, so a motor can start or a valve can open unexpectedly. Force outputs only when the machine and the process have been made safe for exactly that action and nobody is in the danger zone, follow the site's procedures, and remove every force after the test. Forcing in PLC Lab is a simulation and says nothing about whether the same action is safe on real equipment. Active forces are shown in the toolbar and on the FORCE LED.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: Skipping the I/O check because the program 'works in simulation'. Swapped wires and wrong mappings are found here, not later.

question.question: Which step comes before the function test?
question.explanation: Signals must be correct before functions can be tested.

sections.heading: Practice: wrong measuring range
sections.body: A commissioning error makes a level read high. Find and fix the configuration.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
Commission in order, document every check and remove every force.

**Troubleshooting note:** Never leave a force active after a check: a forgotten force is a fault you created.

checkpoint.question: What does an I/O check prove?
options: Each signal reaches the right tag and device

checkpoint.question: What must happen after forcing?
checkpoint.explanation: Forces override the program until removed.
